definition: A particle in the nucleus with a relative charge of $+1$ and a relative mass of 1.
A particle in the nucleus with no charge (relative charge $0$) and a relative mass of 1.
Any particle in the nucleus: a proton or a neutron.
The number of protons in a nucleus, symbol $Z$, also called the atomic number; every atom of an element has the same proton number.
The total number of protons and neutrons in a nucleus, symbol $A$, also called the mass number.
A particular kind of nucleus, with a set number of protons and of neutrons, written in nuclide notation as $^{A}_{Z}\text{X}$.
One of two or more forms of an element whose atoms have the same proton number but different numbers of neutrons.
The splitting of a large nucleus, such as uranium-235, into two smaller nuclei, which releases energy and usually two or three neutrons.
